title: Mutually orthogonal anti-Latin squares
summary: Anti-Latin squares were introduced in connection with non-linear secure network coding, and the extremal problem for large mutually orthogonal families is motivated by that setting. We study the maximum size $N_A(d)$ of a family of mutually orthogonal anti-Latin squares of order $d$. We prove that $N_L(d)+1\le N_A(d)\le N_L(d)+2$ for every $d\ge 3$, where $N_L(d)$ denotes the classical maximum size of a family of mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $d$, and we show that in fact $N_A(3)=N_L(3)+1$ whereas $N_A(d)=N_L(d)+2$ for every $d\ge 4$.
